summary: Todd A. Gibson is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University, attested in 1991, where he studied under György Kara.

Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Theodore Riccardi, Ainslie T. Embree, Morton Klass, Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Frederic B. Underwood, Alex Wayman, and Margaret Mead, later serving at the College of the Holy Cross.

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery (1913–1923) and held posts at Tohoku University (lecturer, ~1925–1944) and the University of Tokyo (~1947–1953).
Tokio Takata (born 1949) specializes in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1968–1972) and later held a post there (~1986–2015).
Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. After studying at Kyoto University (~1934–1937), he served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1955–1983).

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) studied Buddhist studies at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara. He held teaching posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko, and Toyo University (~1887–1898).

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1916–1919). He held positions at Kyoto Institute of Technology, Kyoto University of Education, and Ryukoku University.

Tom J. F. Tillemans (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018) and held the Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary.

Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, UC Santa Barbara, and Yale University, later holding faculty posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1988–2001) and the University of Michigan.
Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto and served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University, both attested in 2012.
Tomoyuki Komine (born 1971) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University, where he also served as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was affiliated with Hiroshima University and the JSPS in 1998, and later served as an associate professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Madras under C. S. Sundaram and Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal, holding a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, William Sax, and Jim Wilson, later holding professorships at Victoria University of Wellington and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Tony K. Stewart (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976) and held faculty positions at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011–2021).

Torkel Brekke (born 1970) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oslo under Jens Braarvig and Georg von Simson, and at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later holding posts at Oxford and Oslo.

Toru Haneda (1882–1955) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907) and held a post at Kyoto University (~1907–1945).
Toru Kumeji specializes in Buddhist studies. He has held positions at the Center for Open Humanities Data and as a senior researcher at the Humanities Information Studies Institute (attested 2015).

Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) was a scholar in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at Keijo Imperial University (~1926–1945) and Tenri University (~1950–1965), founded the Koreanology Association, and taught at Fukuoka University.

Toru Tomabechi (born 1965) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, later holding posts at Lausanne, the Humanities Information Studies Institute, and the Center for Open Humanities Data.
